contract.note: The comparable-work reading is defensible, but the result depends on it. Excluding spending driven by higher quality may cut against the speaker's mechanism, since newer models use more tokens. Read as frontier spending, the claim looks stronger; at fixed performance, costs fall.

evidence.note: A company blog describing why application inference costs rose. It holds neither task nor quality constant, and it is the speaker's own linked source.

Preprint finding: frontier spending is rising, cost at fixed performance is falling, and average SWE-bench prices are roughly flat. The results are mixed depending on reading and do not measure a representative workload.

reviews.rationale: The evidence splits by interpretation. Frontier spending rose, but cost at a fixed performance level fell and average benchmark prices were flat. No representative longitudinal comparison of comparable tasks establishes that total inference cost rose because of reasoning tokens.

semantics.note: This isolates the firm 'no path to profitability' clause. The cash-burn clause is a separate assertion and is reasonably left out. No deadline was stated.

contract.note: Reading 'path' as a credible route to profitability is ordinary. But the evaluator supplies the credibility standard and the profit measure. The 2025 target period is odd for a status claim made at publication, though it is used only as the basis for judging that status.

evidence.note: WSJ report on investor projections: Anthropic breaks even around 2028 and OpenAI turns profitable around 2030. These are management plans that show a route was articulated, but their feasibility is not independently established.
Anthropic's S-1 (October 26, 2026) discloses large net losses and the hedged risk that it may never be profitable. A risk factor neither proves nor rules out a credible route.

reviews.rationale: Management projections show stated profitability targets, and the S-1 shows heavy losses and uncertainty. Neither establishes nor excludes a credible, funded route to profitability for either company as of publication.
